title: Slow-burn GPU exhaustion: queue growth, admission pacing and autoscaler hardening
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Post-incident follow-up for a gradual ("slow-burn") GPU capacity exhaustion that manifested as sustained queue growth over ~18 hours. Root interactions: tenant prefetch behavior + KV-cache eviction churn + autoscaler hysteresis led to progressive queue amplification and repeated throttling. This ticket tracks short- and medium-term mitigations, telemetry gaps, and longer-term autoscaler and admission refactors to prevent recurrence.
acceptance_criteria: Repro harness that exercises slow-burn pattern and validates mitigation reduces sustained queue length by >= 70% under synthetic workload
Admission pacing change deployed to hosted with canary across two GPU pools and validated against live traffic for 48h without false positives
Autoscaler hysteresis and cool-down tuning merged and rolled out; documented expected behavior and thresholds in runbook
Telemetry dashboard surfacing sequence-length distribution, per-tenant prefill rate, KV eviction churn, and queue-growth slope
Runbook updated with operational playbook and emergency backoff endpoint; SLOs for admission/events clarified
work_items: Implement admission-gradient (rate-limited admission that decays with queue slope) — eng/runtime (owner: Diego)
Add sequence-length-aware slot packing to reduce slot waste from long-context requests — eng/packing (owner: Priya)
Introduce KV-cache eviction telemetry (evictions/sec, hot-key churn) and link to tenant metrics — eng/telemetry (owner: Omar)
Tune autoscaler cool-down and prewarm thresholds to avoid oscillation for gradual increases — eng/autoscaler (owner: Lina)
Deploy a tenant-prefill backoff flag to temporarily disable aggressive prefetch during pool stress — eng/cc (owner: Diego)
Create reproducible load generator and CI job that simulates the slow-burn pattern — eng/qe (owner: Marcus)
Add canary config and rollout plan for admission-gradient to hosted control plane — eng/release (owner: Sara)
Update incident runbook, add decision tree and playbook links — eng/sre (owner: Tomás)
postmortem_actions: Root cause: interaction between tenant prefetch (aggressive KV prime) and an eviction policy that regressed (higher churn) during long-tail request patterns — action: revert regression and add regression test
Short-term mitigation: deploy admission-gradient to slow admission when queue slope > threshold; provides immediate deck-stabilization during slow-burn events
Medium-term: autoscaler hysteresis tuning and dynamic prewarm sizing to avoid under/over-scaling oscillations for ramp durations > 15m
Long-term: refactor prefetch subsystem to be pool-aware and signal backoff on elevated eviction churn
Observability: new dashboard and alerts for sustained positive queue slope over 30m, and KV eviction rate crossing tenant-specific baseline
Operational: emergency backoff endpoint for Support to flip tenant prefetch to conservative mode during incidents
Policy: add new standard test case in pre-merge suite that simulates mixed sequence lengths + steady growth to catch regressions
